findings.mechanism: Every command arm strides by the command's arity without checking `args.length % arity`, then asserts the read: src/transform/path.ts:342-343 (`L`: `args[k]!`, `args[k+1]!`), :375-377 (`C`, 6-stride), :392-393 (`S`), :412-413 (`Q`), :427 (`T`), :442-446 (`A`, 7-stride). findings.defect: Compact (unseparated) SVG arc flags are mis-tokenized, producing silently WRONG geometry with no error — and the compact form is what every minifier emits, so this is the common case, not the exotic one. The file's own docstring claims full `A` support including the flags.
findings.evidence: dist/subpaths/transform.js, two spellings of the same circle: expanded `getTotalLength("M 10 10 A 5 5 0 0 1 20 10 A 5 5 0 0 1 10 10")` = 31.403311569547547 (true circumference 2*pi*5 = 31.41592653589793, correct to flattening tolerance); byte-equivalent compact `getTotalLength("M10 10A5 5 0 0120 10A5 5 0 0110 10")` = **0**. Also `getTotalLength("M0 0A1 1 0 011 1")` = 0 vs expanded 1.5701655784773765. SVG 1.1 §8.3.9 grammar: `flag ::= "0" | "1"` — a single character requiring no following separator, which is exactly what SVGO `convertPathData`, Figma and Illustrator emit. Gate block MTS-04, 1 RED.
findings.mechanism: src/transform/path.ts:64 `NUMBER_RE = /-?(?:\d*\.\d+|\d+\.?)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?/g` is applied uniformly to the whole argument run (:86), so `0 0120 10` tokenizes as `[0, 120, 10]` instead of `[0, 0, 1, 20, 10]`. The 7-argument arc run collapses to 6, every argument after the flags shifts one slot, `args[k+6]!` reads `undefined` (the MTS-03 mechanism), `dTheta` becomes NaN, and `segments = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(NaN))` = NaN at :268-271 so the sampling loop at :272 never executes — the arc contributes zero length and the function returns a plausible-looking finite number. That is why it reads as 0 rather than NaN: the corruption is swallowed twice.
findings.waveShape: BUILD, same file and same session as MTS-03. Born-RED gate: block MTS-04 asserts `|expanded - compact| < 1e-6` over the circle pair above; RED today (31.4033 vs 0). Add a fixture set of real minifier output (one SVGO-optimised path) so the gate does not regress to the spelling it was written against. This is the highest-value single fix in transform/: keyframes.js MotionPath/MorphSVG/DrawSVG are the named consumers in the file's own header, and they receive minified path data.

Control identity -> `{scale:[1,1,1], quaternion:[0,0,0,1], …}`. The signature is `(cssValues: Mat4) => DecomposedMatrix3D | null` and the function DOES return null for the two other non-decomposable cases (length !== 16 at :234, singular perspective sub-matrix at :241/:259) — so the null channel is live and this case simply misses it. Gate block MTS-05, 1 RED. Distinct from MT-F019's `decomposeMatrix3D(null)` finding, which is about a signature-violating argument; this input satisfies `Mat4` exactly.
findings.mechanism: src/transform/decompose.ts:281-282 computes `scaleX = vec3Length(...row0)` and immediately divides `row0` by it with no zero test; :293-295 and :314-317 repeat the pattern for scaleY/scaleZ and then divide the skews by them. Downstream: `recomposeMatrix3D` of that object yields all-NaN, and `interpolateDecomposed` (:577-601) lerps NaN through both operands, so one degenerate matrix silently voids an entire interpolation.

findings.evidence: dist/subpaths/math.js: `deCasteljau(0.5, [])` -> `undefined`, declared `number`; `interpBezier(0.5, [])` -> `[undefined, undefined]`, declared `readonly [number, number]`; `lerpArray(new Float64Array([1,2,3]), new Float64Array([4,5]), 0.5, new Float64Array(3))` -> `[2.5, 3.5, NaN]` — silent, no throw, no signal. `scale(5,3,3)` throws `Error: fromMax and fromMin cannot be equal`, i.e. the one bare-throw in the subpath, and it is thrown AFTER the division it exists to prevent. Gate block MTS-06, 3 RED. `dist/subpaths/math.d.ts` is the only .d.ts in the package with zero unexported declares — the surface is clean; the semantics are not.
findings.mechanism: src/foundation/math.ts:95 `return b[0]!` — for `points = []`, `n = -1`, the loops never run and the assertion hands back `undefined` as `number`; :107-110 `points.map((xy) => xy[0]!)` propagates it into `interpBezier`. :69 `out[i] = u * start[i]! + t * stop[i]!` — a Float64Array OOB read is `undefined`, so `t * undefined` is NaN, and an OOB WRITE is a silent no-op; the docstring at :58 states the length contract in prose ("`start`, `stop`, `out` must share the same length") and nothing enforces it. :15 computes `slope = (toMax-toMin)/(fromMax-fromMin)` three lines BEFORE the `fromMax === fromMin` guard at :18. These are 7 of the 297 assertions, and unlike decompose.ts's 113 the array lengths here are entirely caller-controlled.
findings.waveShape: BUILD. Two acts, both completable in one session: (1) length-precondition on `lerpArray` and an empty-points precondition on `deCasteljau`/`interpBezier` — throw a named Error or return NaN explicitly, but choose ONE and state it in the docstring that currently states an unenforced contract; (2) move the `scale` guard above the division. Born-RED gate: block MTS-06 asserts finiteness on all three — RED today 3/3. Coordination weight, and the reason this is MAJOR not MINOR: keyframes.js imports ./math at 8 sites and `lerpArray` is its J.W6-adopted FrameCompiler hot loop driving one call per playhead sample — a mis-sized buffer there yields NaN animation frames with no diagnostic, and keyframes' own `lerparray-adopt.test.ts` locks the API and the `(1-t)a+tb` semantics but not the length precondition.

Its true starting position is not "harmonize two API shapes" — it is a four-major migration across a DELETED entry point and a DELETED symbol. No formation document read this session states this.

All five fourier import sites use the bare root specifier: `web/src/lib/easings.ts:9` and `:16`, `web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:5`, `web/src/components/equation/lib/harmonics.ts:5`, `web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:8`. Of the two symbols named, `easeInOutSine` survives but only under `./easing` (src/subpaths/easing.ts), and `timingFunctions` returns ZERO hits across all of `src/` and `dist/subpaths/` — it does not exist in 4.0.0 under any subpath.
findings.mechanism: Two independent breaks stacked. (1) The root export was removed between 0.13.0 and 4.0.0; every bare-specifier import in fourier becomes an unresolvable module against the new exports map — Node and Vite both hard-fail, there is no fallback. (2) `timingFunctions` was renamed or absorbed (the nearest 4.0.0 surface is `bezierPresets` + `easing(name)` on `./easing`), so even after re-pointing the specifier one of the two call sites will not compile. Structurally this is the mirror of MT-F018's keyframes finding: keyframes pins value.js at exactly `4.0.0` and is therefore CURRENT-and-frozen, while fourier carries a caret on a version four majors stale and is therefore SILENTLY-frozen — the caret reads as "tracking" and is doing the opposite.
findings.waveShape: BUILD, and it must be the FIRST act of the A-band isomorphism work, before any API-shape design. Concretely: (a) re-point the five specifiers to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`; (b) resolve `timingFunctions` to its 4.0.0 successor and record the mapping; (c) bump the pin. Born-RED gate, runnable from the fourier tree: `cd fourier-analysis/web && npm i @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 && npx tsc --noEmit` — RED today on 5 unresolved specifiers plus 1 missing export. Note for scope: MT-F018 established the isomorphism spans a language boundary (fourier's `api/` is Python, `web/` is the only TS consumer) — so the surface to be made isomorphic is exactly these five sites plus whatever the Python side re-implements, which is a far smaller and more completable object than "Value/Fourier API isomorphism" suggests.

findings.defect: The general CSS-value serializer is not on the public surface, so the library can parse a stylesheet into a `CssValue` tree and cannot serialize one back — and the downstream consumer forked its own copy, which has since DIVERGED. Two libraries, one AST, two different output strings.
findings.evidence: `serializeCssValue` is declared `export function` at src/css/stylesheet.ts:81 but is absent from src/css/index.ts:51-60, hence absent from `./css`. Verified on the built artifact: `"serializeCssValue" in CSS === false`, while `"serializeCssColor" in CSS === true` and `serializeTimelineOptions` is exported — so the surface exports two narrow serializers and withholds the general one. keyframes.js re-implemented it at `src/animation/compile/emit/css-text.ts:41`. Divergence measured by running both implementations over the SAME parsed tree from `dist/subpaths/css.js`: input `"a : b"` -> value.js `"a: b"`, keyframes `"a : b"`; input `"x ; y"` -> value.js `"x; y"`, keyframes `"x ; y"`; control `"1px 2px"` -> identical. Gate block MTS-08, 1 RED. Same pattern for `serializeKeyframeSelector` (src/css/grammar.ts:429, unexported, reachable only by the deep src import at test/v4-c1.test.ts:9) vs keyframes' `serializeSelector` at css-text.ts:58.
findings.mechanism: The barrel at src/css/index.ts enumerates its re-exports by hand rather than star-forwarding, so an `export` in a leaf module does not reach the subpath — and nothing checks the two lists against each other. value.js's copy applies `result.replace(/\s+([:;])/g, "$1")` to space-separated lists (stylesheet.ts:92); keyframes' copy has no such normalization. Because `parseCssValue` tokenizes `:` and `;` into standalone keyword scalars (`splitValueTokens`, grammar.ts:117-119), any declaration value containing a top-level colon or semicolon — `grid-area`, `@supports` conditions, custom-property payloads — round-trips to two different strings depending on which library serializes it. Aggravating: value.js's copy THROWS a bare `TypeError` at :86 on an unserializable colour, making it the only throwing function in `src/css/` and one that `parseStylesheet` calls internally at :500, :652, :657, :665 and :709-717.
findings.waveShape: BUILD — a public-surface wave, small and completable. (1) Export `serializeCssValue` and `serializeKeyframeSelector` from src/css/index.ts and src/subpaths/css.ts; (2) convert the :86 throw to the module's own `Result`/failure idiom before publishing it, since publishing a throwing serializer from a "failure-explicit" package repeats MT-F024's contract violation in the opposite direction; (3) relay to keyframes.js (E13) to delete its fork and adopt — this is the exact shape of the SCI-1 additive-API ask (DR-21) and should be landed in the same packet. Born-RED gate: block MTS-08 asserts `"serializeCssValue" in CSS` — RED today. Add a differential gate: parse a fixture corpus, serialize with both implementations, assert byte equality — RED today at 2 of 3 fixtures.

It is referenced by the public surface at :81 (`coerceToSyntax(...): ParseResult<CssValue>`), :132, :149, :155, :203, :210, :221 and by `parseCssValue`/`parseCssValues`. Census across the package: css.d.ts carries **18** unexported declares (Alpha, Alpha_2, AnyColor, Channel, Channel_2, ChannelsBySpace, ChannelsBySpace_2, Color, Color_2, ColorIssue, CssCall, CssList, CssScalar, CssValue, JumpPosition, Result, SpaceId, SpaceId_2), quantize.d.ts 6, value.d.ts 6, color.d.ts 1, easing.d.ts 1; math.d.ts and transform.d.ts are clean at 0. Gate block MTS-09, 1 RED. Companion dead row: `ColorFactory` is exported at src/color/index.ts:7, dropped by src/subpaths/color.ts, and emitted as `declare type ColorFactory` at dist/subpaths/color.d.ts:37 — so a consumer cannot name the type of `rgb`, `oklch`, or any of the 17 factories.
findings.mechanism: src/css/types.ts:131 DOES re-export the six types (`export type { ColorIssue, Result, JumpPosition, CssList, CssScalar, CssValue }`), but src/css/index.ts:1-35 enumerates its forwards by hand and drops all six — so types.ts:131 is dead at the package boundary. The hand-maintained barrel is the same mechanism as MTS-08: two lists that must agree, with nothing checking that they do. The defect survives because TypeScript is structural — a consumer who imports `CssValue` from `./value` gets a compatible type — so the only observable symptom is that the type is unnameable from the subpath that returns it, and `--noEmit` on the consumer stays green.

findings.evidence: `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` emits BOTH copies of five declarations under mangled names — `Alpha_2`, `Channel_2`, `ChannelsBySpace_2`, `Color_2`, `SpaceId_2` — with 25 `_2` references across the file. css.d.ts is 382 lines of the package's 940-line total .d.ts surface (color 111, transform 182, easing 89, value 68, quantize 62, math 46). Import-path census in src/: five modules reach colour types through the implementation (`src/css/grammar.ts:18` and `:19`, `src/css/types.ts:1`, `src/color/anchors.ts:1`, `src/color/operations.ts:15` — all `from "…/color/model"`), while `src/value.ts:1` reaches the same declarations through the barrel (`from "./color/index"`), and `src/subpaths/color.ts:13,38` uses the barrel too.
findings.mechanism: `src/color/index.ts` re-exports from `./model`, so `Color`/`Alpha`/`Channel`/`ChannelsBySpace`/`SpaceId` are reachable by two distinct module specifiers. `src/css/types.ts` imports them one way and `src/value.ts` the other; because `src/css/index.ts` transitively pulls both, the dts rollup sees two module identities for one declaration set and cannot dedupe, so it emits both and disambiguates with `_2`. Not a correctness defect — the types are structurally identical — but it is measurable topology drift and it is the same hand-maintained-barrel discipline failure as MTS-08 and MTS-09, which is why it should be cured with them rather than separately.
